system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Wattlebridge playbook, compared against the Seller's untrusted update and Disclosure Letter
**Date note:** The Disclosure Letter speaks "as at 22 September 2026". Today is 5 November 2026, so the factual statements are about six weeks old. We should ask the Seller to bring every item up to date (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and the bonuses) before we rely on any of them.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of the price (AUD 4,800,000), clause 12.1.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is our fallback, but Amelia Frost has not given prior written authority for this draft. A number matching our fallback does not authorise it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis of AUD 25,000. Basket of AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of AUD 5,000. Basket of AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** The de minimis is five times ours, the basket is five times ours, and the deductible structure would leave the first AUD 250,000 of loss with us permanently.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion. The Seller also wants any limitation to apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject and hold at 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The default wording would quietly pull Fundamental, Tax and IP claims and the indemnities into the general limits.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties to carry the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay for. Capping them at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m price is not an administrative matter.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express carve-out.** This point is non-negotiable under the playbook, and no one on the deal team has authority to waive it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room as at 22 September 2026, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2). DL 1.4 adds a broad non-admission.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific and fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** **Strike DL 1.1 and 1.2. Limit disclosure to the specific items in sections 2–10.** Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure would wipe out the warranties. The specific items are useful to us because they confirm the gaps listed below.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records (clause 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier should rest on named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete clause 8.3.** It combines constructive knowledge with deemed disclosure. Any knowledge qualifier must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or the specific indemnities.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Described as "addressed". Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the written consent. DL 2 admits there is no final consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent, plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied, before Completion. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m and roughly 30% of FY26 revenue.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Make it a hard Completion condition: an effective consent with clause 11.3 conditions evidenced. Bluefen is a material customer, so reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are insufficient, and "addressed" is contradicted by the Seller's own disclosure.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release to be provided after Completion. DL 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Require a payout letter dated close to Completion, payment straight to Riverlark from the funds flow, and executed releases delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and we have neither.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item or funded by the Seller.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Add a named funds-flow line, or a Seller-funded deduction, covering the bonuses and on-costs, backed by a specific indemnity. The Company will owe these amounts, so a statement that they are "for the Seller" is not a mechanism to pay them.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering all losses from defective transfer or ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials, including third-party claims. It should keep the cure route: cleared payment of the SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Broaden the indemnity and require cure evidence.** DL 4 confirms there is no payment receipt and no assignment in the data room. The AUD 180,000 open balance is unverified either way, so we should not treat it as either the cap or the full exposure.

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material" (clause 4.6 / Schedule 6). DL 6 says the investigation is preliminary, with about 1,240 records potentially affected and access, scope and notification all unresolved.
- **Buyer wants:** Logs preserved, the investigation continued, and regular updates to the Buyer, without prejudging the outcome.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the Seller's "not material" characterisation, and do not overstate the matter.** Add covenants for log preservation, investigation and updates, plus a specific warranty or indemnity framework. Treat the matter as unconfirmed: there is no established breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure in either direction.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL 8 is silent on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of these renewals, with no automatic classification either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Hold the position open and request DD-008 and DD-011 terms, timing and accrual status.** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is an unsupported assertion, but we should not convert the amount into Debt or a price deduction without facts.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A blanket application of limitations to "all Claims" (clauses 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5). Fundamental claims are folded into the general regime, and Tax and IP are called "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants and other covenants kept as separate categories, with no hidden override from the general regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Add an express clause stating that the general limits do not apply to Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnity, payment or covenant claims unless the SPA expressly says so. The Seller's drafting achieves the opposite result.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL 10 concedes this is only the source relied on and is not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority.
- **Recommendation:** **Not satisfied.** Require ASIC extracts, PPSR searches, the constitution and share-issue history, board and shareholder approvals, and the Riverlark security releases. An internal register supplied by the Seller does not prove its own accuracy.

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** These are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** The terms treated as OPEN, not resolved, and not assumed to carry unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "settled" label and keep both items on the open-issues list.** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process. We should not concede the general cap for these items, and we should not assume unlimited liability either.

---

### Other points for the team
- **Unverified labels:** We should not adopt any of the Seller's labels ("fair and balanced", "addressed", "agreed price mechanics", "adequate", "settled", "ordinary course") on their face. None of them is a verified fact or an agreed position.
- **Approvals:** Neither fallback (the 20% cap or the 18-month period) may be offered unless Amelia Frost gives written authority that identifies this draft.
- **Office lease and Mossvale:** On the Seller's own disclosure, the office lease (DL 7) needs only a notification and Mossvale (DL 9) is an assignment restriction rather than a change-of-control trigger. We should confirm both by reading the provisions themselves and add the lease notification as a covenant. Neither item is in the playbook issue list.
=== END ADVICE ===
